props.name: series A particle surfaces are enriched in chromic acid
props.statement: In catalysts A the chromic-acid-rich liquid of the paste left, on drying, a surface layer of higher chromic acid content, so the particle surface is richer in chromic acid than the interior and the bulk composition of A does not indicate the real surface concentration; the composition of B does, since B is made from the solid free of liquid.

props.name: activity rises to an asymptotic maximum at Cr/Zn 0.5 (series B)
props.statement: Only series B (made from the solid free of liquid) gives the correct relation of composition to activity: activity rises with chromic acid content to an asymptotic maximum at Cr/Zn = 0.5; series A shows maximum synthesis activity at a Cr/Zn a little below 0.5, and B-10 (Cr/Zn 0.5) is more active than A-7 of the same ratio.

props.name: low-Cr catalysts are contaminated by carbon from CO decomposition
props.statement: Catalysts without or with a little chromic acid turned gray after a few days of synthesis and then gave far lower methanol-decomposition activity, whereas those with higher chromic acid content neither darkened nor lost activity: the surface of the former is more easily contaminated with carbon from carbon monoxide decomposition during the synthesis.

props.name: chromic acid improves selectivity and prevents CO decomposition
props.statement: Within the range studied, hardly any effect of chromic acid addition undesirable to the selectivity of the synthesis was found; by-products were very small (CO2 increase ≤ 1%, hardly any methane, formaldehyde 0.1%, methyl formate 0.5%), and the water yield, highest on the zinc oxide catalyst, falls rapidly with Cr/Zn. The authors emphasize the improvement of selectivity and the prevention of carbon monoxide decomposition by chromic acid, suggestive of an intracrystalline promoting effect.

props.name: nitrate coprecipitation gave no homogeneous, moderately active catalyst
props.statement: A catalyst prepared by coprecipitation of zinc and chromium hydroxides from a mixed nitrate solution proved difficult to obtain with homogeneous structure and moderate activity.

props.name: activity parallels surface area: intercrystalline promotion
props.statement: The catalytic activity of catalysts of different Cr/Zn almost parallels their specific surface area, and the activity per unit surface area changes far less than the activity per unit mass: this suggests an apparent proportionality of activity to surface area and, with the relation of surface area to Cr/Zn, an intercrystalline promoting effect of chromic acid.

props.name: chromic acid is also an intracrystalline promoter
props.statement: Chromic acid lowers both the frequency factor and the activation energy (per unit surface area) toward those of catalyst S, presumably a zinc chromite spinel, so the specific activity is maintained at the level of S; chromic acid behaves not only as an intercrystalline (structural) promoter but also as an intracrystalline promoter, modifying the catalyst structure advantageously for preserving the specific activity.

props.name: the maximum shortly before Cr/Zn 0.5 is not a necessary relation
props.statement: For that reason, the activity maximum at a Cr/Zn ratio shortly before 0.5, usual in previous work, is not the necessary relation between activity and chemical composition; an exact representation of the activity change in the intermediate range of Cr/Zn is not yet established.

props.name: paste solid holds at most Cr/Zn 0.5
props.statement: The solid in the paste (catalyst B) can contain no more chromic acid than that equivalent to Cr/Zn = 0.5; it is in equilibrium with a liquid of higher chromic acid concentration whose amount increases with the chromic acid content of the paste (paste 1/3 to 2.0: solid 0.31 to 0.50, liquid 0.82 to 1.95). Two hours of kneading at most complete the reaction and give a solid of homogeneous structure.

props.name: surface area max at Cr/Zn 0.4 in A; B larger than A
props.statement: In series A the specific surface area (after synthesis) passes through a maximum at Cr/Zn = 0.4; the catalysts of series B have larger specific surface areas than the corresponding ones of series A.

props.name: clean low-Cr catalysts would show falling specific synthesis activity with Cr
props.statement: If the catalyst surface remained clean, catalysts with no or little chromic acid would show a downward tendency of (specific) synthesis activity with increasing chromic acid content; the observed rise at low Cr/Zn reflects carbon contamination. The trends of activation energy and frequency factor may be considered inherent to the clean surface although the syntheses were not always on a clean surface.

props.name: difference from Frolich et al. due to preparation
props.note: Molstad's and Frolich's results are cited, not this source's tests.
props.statement: The present maximum activity lies at the same Cr/Zn ratio as found by Molstad et al. but at a somewhat higher ratio than found by Frolich et al.; the difference may mainly be due to the different mode of catalyst preparation.

props.name: excessive chromic acid may lower activity
props.statement: An excessive addition of chromic acid may certainly decrease the activity, since chromic acid alone is no more an active catalyst than zinc oxide alone.
